snp4.15:1.1:
“When embraced,
the rod of violence
breeds danger & fear:
snp4.15:2.3:
competing with one another—
as I saw this,
snp4.15:3.1:
The world was entirely
without substance.
snp4.15:3.2:
All the directions
were knocked out of line.
snp4.15:3.4: I saw nothing that wasn’t laid claim to.
snp4.15:4.1:
Seeing nothing in the end
but competition,
snp4.15:4.3:
And then I saw
an arrow here,
snp4.15:4.4:
so very hard to see,
embedded in the heart.
snp4.15:5.3: But simply on pulling it out
snp4.15:5.4:
you don’t run,
you don’t sink.
snp4.15:6.2: Whatever things are tied down in the world,
snp4.15:6.3: you shouldn’t be set on them.
snp4.15:6.4:
Having totally penetrated
sensual pleasures,
sensual passions,
snp4.15:6.5:
you should train for your own
unbinding.
snp4.15:7.3:
Without anger, the sage
should cross over
snp4.15:8.3:
shouldn’t stand firm in his pride—
the man with his heart set
on unbinding.
snp4.15:10.4:
get entangled in
what’s dazzling & bright.
snp4.15:11.1:
I call greed
a great flood;
snp4.15:11.4:
sensuality, a bog
hard to cross over.
snp4.15:12.2:
a sage stands on high ground
: a brahman.
snp4.15:12.4:
he is said to be
at peace;
snp4.15:13.1:
having clearly known, he
is an attainer-of-knowledge;
snp4.15:14.1:
Whoever here has gone beyond
sensual passions—
snp4.15:14.2:
an attachment hard
to transcend in the world—
snp4.15:14.4:
He, his stream cut, is free
from bonds.
snp4.15:15.3:
If you don’t grasp
at what’s in between,
snp4.15:16.1:
For whom, in name-&-form,
in every way,
there’s no sense of mine,
snp4.15:16.3:
and who doesn’t grieve
over what is not:
snp4.15:16.4:
He, in the world,
isn’t defeated,
suffers no loss.
snp4.15:17.2:
‘This is mine,’
for whom nothing is others’:
snp4.15:17.3: He, feeling no sense of mine-ness,
snp4.15:17.4:
doesn’t grieve at the thought
‘I have nothing.’
snp4.15:18.3:
This is the reward
—I say when asked—
for those who are free
from theorizing.
snp4.15:20.1:
The sage
doesn’t speak of himself
snp4.15:20.2:
as among those who are higher,
equal,
or lower.
